text: When designing a REST API, clarity and consistency are key. Each resource should have a clear, logical endpoint, such as `/users` or `/orders`, using nouns instead of verbs. Always use standard HTTP status codes to communicate results—for example, `200` for success, `201` for creation, `404` for not found, and `500` for server errors. Good documentation is essential, as it helps other developers understand how to use your API without guessing. Finally, plan for the future by using versioning, like `/v1/users`. This way, when you make changes, existing users won’t suddenly have their applications break. Simple, predictable design saves everyone time.
